# Element Module Skeleton Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Create the `src/element/` module tree so the sealed element-trait hierarchy can be built in later tasks without introducing a second sealing mechanism.

**Architecture:** `src/element/mod.rs` owns the public trait surface and re-exports; `primitives.rs` hosts concrete impls; `numeric.rs`, `real.rs`, and `complex.rs` host the capability traits. All public element traits must reuse `crate::private::Sealed`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.85+, edition 2024, std

**Design Docs:** `design/03-element.md` §3 (file layout), `design/03-element.md` §4 (dependencies), `design/03-element.md` §5.7 (shared Sealed strategy), `design/01-architecture.md` §3 (repository structure)

**Prerequisites:** W1T4 and W1T3 must be complete.

---

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the complete skeleton files**

Create `src/element/mod.rs` with the following content:

```rust
//! Element trait hierarchy for Xenon's closed element set.
//!
//! Supported types are `i32`, `i64`, `f32`, `f64`, `Complex<f32>`,
//! `Complex<f64>`, and `bool`.

use crate::private::Sealed;

mod complex;
mod numeric;
mod primitives;
mod real;

pub(crate) use Sealed as ElementSealed;
```
